description: A veteran Chinese literary-historical journalist's documentary account of the hidden front of the Chinese Communist Party: the intelligence and internal-security services that grew up alongside its army, from the "special work" cells born of the 1927 terror through the Central Special Branch, the wartime spy duels with the Nationalists and the Japanese, the excesses of the Yan'an "Rescue Campaign," and the transformation of a clandestine party apparatus into the public-security organs of a new state. Built on the author's interviews with hundreds of surviving intelligence and security veterans.
_translator_note: Optional. A list of paragraph strings rendered verbatim as the Translator's Note back-matter page. Inline ... is honored; use NUMERIC character references (— em dash,   nbsp), never named entities. If omitted, a generic method note is generated.
translator_note: This is an English translation of 中国秘密战：中共情报、保卫工作纪实 (China's Secret War: A Documentary Record of the CCP's Intelligence and Security Work) by Hao Zaijin, prepared from an image-only scan with no digital text layer.

The book is reportage (报告文学), not academic history: it is built on the author's own interviews with surviving intelligence and security veterans and is told in a brisk, colloquial, frequently editorializing voice. That voice has been kept. Where the book's factual claims can be checked against the documentary record, the footnotes say whether the account is corroborated, uncorroborated, or contradicted; where it reflects the author's political vantage as a sympathetic insider, the notes say so.

Chinese personal and place names use pinyin except for forms with a settled English convention. Intelligence-service terms (中统, 军统, 中央特科, 社会部) are glossed at first appearance and listed in the glossary. Footnotes cite the book's own printed page numbers. Damaged or uncertain readings from the scan are flagged honestly rather than smoothed over.
source_note: Image-only PDF scan, 436 pages, no text layer (Internet Archive, from Contra Costa County Library). Simplified Chinese, horizontal, left-to-right. Structure: cover and title/CIP pages (PDF 1-4); a photo-plate section interleaved with the printed table of contents (PDF 5-32, its own folio sequences); Preface 前言 探秘 (PDF 33-35, own sequence, printed 1-3); body 12 chapters / 86 numbered sections (PDF 37-430, printed 1-394, offset constant: printed = pdf - 36); a source-note / interviewee section and the Afterword 后记 (PDF 427-434, printed ~391-398); library endpapers (PDF 435-436). The book carries its OWN apparatus of source notes citing the author's interviews; detect and handle with detect_notes.py at batch time. Verso pages print a vertical running title in the outer (left) margin; crop before OCR. This is the '最新升级图文版' (newest upgraded illustrated edition).
_offset_note: The PDF-page-to-printed-folio offset usually DRIFTS as unpaginated plates accumulate. Do NOT use a constant formula. Record per-section pdf_page/printed_page anchors below and READ the folio off the scan at each opener.
_end_note: The last PDF page and printed folio of the body text. Set these so the LAST chapter's/section's page length is known in the survey; without them its length shows as '?'.
_structure_note: One entry per chapter, in reading order. Each chapter: id (ch01..), chapter (int), title (zh), title_en, pdf_page + printed_page of its opener, and a sections list. OPTIONAL 'part': a label like 'Part One. ...' — consecutive chapters sharing a part are grouped under it in the TOC. Each section: id (ch01s01..), section (int), title (zh), title_en, pdf_page, printed_page, and an OPTIONAL 'subsections' list (id ch01s01x1.., title, title_en, pdf_page, printed_page). The reading markdown uses '## ' for the chapter (h1), '### ' per section (h2, matched to these section ids in order), '#### ' per subsection (h3, matched to the subsection ids in order). Fill in the WHOLE structure up front (from the TOC or PDF bookmarks): the survey and the skeleton EPUB are built from it before any translation.
